page: Amazon Web Services c8i.xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical Intel Xeon 6975P-C cores, running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The processor includes 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a large 480 MB L3 cache. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, and it offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core performance, with the Geekbench single-core score and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core scaling presents a tradeoff; both stress-ng multi-core performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is mixed, with large-block read and write bandwidth scoring in the middle 50%, while cached small-block read bandwidth and the PassMark memory score rank in the bottom 25%.

The hardware profile is tailored for compute-bound tasks that benefit from high single-core execution speeds and advanced instruction sets, such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. Qualitative cost efficiency is driven by the dedicated CPU allocation and high-speed DDR5 memory, though the low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2 GB per core limits its utility for memory-intensive applications. It is suitable for workloads such as single-threaded data processing, lightweight web serving, software compilation, and basic text processing.
